subject: Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?
parts: I'm looking to explore using stan for real-time bayesian estimation of gaze position during eye tracking. As the data streams in, I'll need to use the posterior from analysis of y[i-1] as the prior for datum y[i]. Is there a way to directly provide samples as priors rather than the more typical specification of distributions?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?
parts:
The simple answer is "no" --- we can't use a sample as a prior.

Your best estimate for theta[i] is what it is with data items y[1], ..., y[i],
but when you see y[i+1], you don't want to freeze theta[1], ..., theta[i] --- that's the
cut behavior of BUGS. Rather, you want to estimate them jointly given all
the data y[1], ..., y[i+1].

What do you mean by "real time"? If you're looking at something with millisecond
responsiveness, I doubt Stan's going to be the right tool no matter what you do.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?
parts:
Bob:

I think you’re misinterpreting the question. “Cut” has nothing to do with it and I think that was an inrrelevant distraction I agree that, from the context, it seems that Mike Lawrence is interestied in estimaing a stream of thetas (“gaze positions”), but I see no evidence that he wants to freeze the estimates of thetas based on past data. I assume he wants to _update_ the estimate of thetas as new data come in.

As we’ve discussed in the Stan meetings, I do think this could be posssible in some way—it reminds me a lot of adiabatic Monte Carlo. I agree with you that we don’t have anything in Stan to do it now, but it definitlely should be on our long-term agenda. And it could well be that, if someone wants to implement something in R or Py or Julia or whatever to do this sort of computation, that Stan could be a component in this.

A

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?
parts:
Like Andrew said — continued updating is problematic with MCMC because
samples do not a distribution make. The go-to algorithm these days is
Sequential Monte Carlo, which is usually implemented with particles a la
particle filtering (the particle updates could be implemented with Adiabatic
Monte Carlo if the updating is particularly onerous). You could use parts
of the Stan API to implement SMC but such an algorithm wouldn’t be in
Stan for a long time, if ever, as there are lots of complications to the
algorithm that prevent automated implementations.

Also, in my experience trying to approximate the posterior with a normal
(even a multivariate normal) rarely works for models with any nontrivial
structure.

Stochastic VB uses streaming data to estimate parameters that define
an approximating density (usually a normal). It’s more robust than using
the empirical means/covariance to define a normal after each update,
but can still be tricky to implement for a general model.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Real-time data analysis: using posterior samples as prior for new data?
parts:
On Apr 27, 2015, at 12:25 PM, Andrew Gelman <Gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>
> Bob:
>
> I think you’re misinterpreting the question.
Maybe because it came with a suggested implementation. See below.

> “Cut” has nothing to do with it and I think that was an inrrelevant distraction I agree that, from the context, it seems that Mike Lawrence is interestied in estimaing a stream of thetas (“gaze positions”), but I see no evidence that he wants to freeze the estimates of thetas based on past data. I assume he wants to _update_ the estimate of thetas as new data come in.

If you use the draws from the theta[1] ... theta[n] as priors for theta[n+1],
then it doesn't seem like you're going to update theta[1], ..., theta[n].
Also, a single pass of filtering won't update them either unless you go back
to the beginning and resample earlier parameters.

> As we’ve discussed in the Stan meetings, I do think this could be posssible in some way—it reminds me a lot of adiabatic Monte Carlo. I agree with you that we don’t have anything in Stan to do it now, but it definitlely should be on our long-term agenda.

Agreed.

- Bob
